stories.title: Quantification and classification of carbon nanotubes in electron micrographs using vision foundation models
stories.description: Accurate characterization of carbon nanotube morphologies in electron microscopy images is vital for exposure assessment and toxicological studies, yet current workflows rely on slow, subjective manual segmentation. This work presents a unified framework that leverages vision foundation models to automate the quantification and classification of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) in electron microscopy images. First, an interactive quantification tool built on the Segment Anything Model segments particles with near-perfect accuracy using minimal user input. Second, a classification pipeline uses the resulting masks to spatially constrain a DINOv2 vision transformer, extracting features exclusively from particle regions while suppressing background noise. Evaluated on a dataset of approximately 1800 TEM images, the architecture achieves 89.5% cross-validated accuracy and 92.7% on a held-out test set in distinguishing four CNT morphologies, outperforming the previous baseline while using a fraction of the training data. Instance-level processing enables the framework to resolve mixed samples, correctly classifying distinct particle types co-existing within a single field of view. These results demonstrate that integrating zero-shot segmentation with self-supervised feature learning enables high-throughput, reproducible nanomaterial analysis, transforming a labor-intensive bottleneck into a scalable, data-driven process.
